body.heading: The hidden ledger
paragraphs: Many of us keep quiet accounts: I drove last time, I paid for the last two coffees, I always host. The ledger feels like fairness, but it slowly turns every kindness into a transaction waiting to be settled.
Scorekeeping also backfires: the other person rarely knows the tally, so the resentment arrives as a surprise. Most 'sudden' friendship rifts are ledgers finally being read aloud.

body.heading: Giving with open hands
paragraphs: Share what you can genuinely afford — time, food, a ride, a spare ticket — and let it be gone. If you cannot afford it, decline warmly rather than give with a hook in it.
Strangely, people who share without scoring tend to receive more, not less: generosity without pressure is the kind people love to return, in their own time and their own way.

description: Generosity with a ledger attached is a loan in disguise. Sharing freely is simpler — and strangely easier to sustain.
